# Grind Log

> A record of one speedrunner's Ninja Gaiden (NES) Any% attempts, read off the
> public Twitch broadcast frame by frame by an OCR bot: every attempt, its
> death or finish time, per-act splits, the runner's own attempt numbers, and
> capture health per day. Rendered at https://ng.lexicone.com/.

## Data

Static JSON, rebuilt every 10 minutes while a stream is live, nightly, and
after each VOD import; served with an ETag and `Cache-Control: max-age=60`
(the docs and schema 3600; a closed day file of the per-day feed
`max-age=60, s-maxage=31536000`, a year at the edge, invalidated on change).

- https://ng.lexicone.com/api/v1/latest.json — state of the grind in ~3 KB:
  today, records (season best, best tracked, Sum of Best, references), the
  last run and last finish, streaks, golds, deaths by act. Poll this.
- https://ng.lexicone.com/api/v1/summary.json — every aggregate the site
  shows (~35 KB): daily rows with the runner's attempt-number span, all
  finishes, PB history, golds, death chart, sessions with capture health.
- https://ng.lexicone.com/api/v1/report.json — everything (~1 MB, ~85 KB
  gzipped): every run with its outcome and times, per-run splits, sessions.
- https://ng.lexicone.com/api/v1/index.json — manifest with byte sizes and
  the build time.
- https://ng.lexicone.com/api/v1/manifest.json — the per-day feed, for a
  reader that keeps a copy: lists `days/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json` (every run of one
  day with its splits, the day's sessions and capture health) with size,
  sha256 and whether the day is closed, plus the records to beat with their
  scope and source. A closed day changes rarely but does change (a VOD
  import renumbers attempt_number database-wide; run numbers get filled in
  later): the sha256 is the only truth. Run ids are the start time in ms and
  survive re-imports of the same VOD, but a live day replaced by its VOD is
  re-keyed — key on (day, id) and resync a day whose sha256 changed.
  `history.json` is the per-day stats and every finish without the runs;
  `schema.json` the JSON Schema. Fetch the manifest, then only the days
  whose sha256 differs from your copy.
- https://ng.lexicone.com/api/v1/README.md — the field reference.

## Caveats

- Every time was read off the video by OCR. The timer reader is accurate to
  the hundredth on well over 99% of frames; a finish is the timer frozen for
  several frames, so finish times are exact to the display.
- Days are the streamer's local day (`timezone` in each file). `today` is the
  day at build time: after the nightly build it is the day that just closed
  until the next live build. Check `today.day`.
- Two attempt numbers exist. `livesplit_attempt` is the runner's own counter
  read off the layout and is the run's identity; `tracked_ordinal` is the
  bot's count of what it saw. Prefer the former; it is null when unread.
- "Season best" is the runner's comparison, which resets with each season of
  his splits file; the lifetime PB and the world record are `references`.
